**Tenure/timeline notes:** Left her most recent long-term role (Program Manager, 16 months) due to a family member's health situation - a clear, reasonable explanation.
**Recommendation:** Hold/comment - she's the only applicant so far and brings real behavioral-health program depth, but the core outreach/BD/referral-development experience genuinely isn't there; worth a phone screen to gauge transferability rather than a decision either way, since nothing here is a "wrong field" red flag, just a different specialization.

name: Sameer Eric
review:
**Fit summary:** Not a fit - lacks the hard licensure requirement entirely and the background is sales, not clinical.
**Strengths:** One year as a Behavioral Health Technician / RADT license holder shows some direct-care exposure.
**Gaps:** No active FL LMHC/LCSW/LMFT license (RADT is a recovery/addiction detox technician credential, not a therapy license, and the posting requires "Active, full Florida licensure as an LMHC, LCSW, or LMFT"); no Spanish fluency against an explicit requirement; primary career is financial brokerage and sales, not clinical intake or adolescent PHP/IOP work; comp ask ($30/hr) doesn't reflect the $35/hr posted rate context either way.
**Recommendation:** Disqualify - wrong field entirely relative to a role requiring an active clinical license, adolescent PHP/IOP experience, and bilingual fluency; none of the three are present.

name: Cyrena McFarlane
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong clinical background working with children, but two open questions on the role's hardest requirements: license type and Spanish fluency.
**Strengths:** Specialist in School Psychology conducting psychoeducational and safety-related evaluations; prior Mental Health Therapist role delivering individual telehealth therapy to 15 children weekly; strong, specific self-described growth area (prioritization/boundaries) suggesting real self-awareness.
**Gaps:** Credential attached appears to be a school-psychology certification, not confirmation of an active FL LMHC/LCSW/LMFT - the posting is explicit that "registered intern or provisional status does not meet the licensure requirement," so this needs direct verification, not an assumption either way [VERIFY]; "No Spanish fluency" against an explicit bilingual requirement; no PHP/IOP-specific admissions/intake experience (her settings are schools and telehealth therapy, not treatment-program intake).
**Consistency check:** None apparent - resume and questionnaire align (still employed, explains why).
**Tenure/timeline notes:** Stable, sequential roles with no gaps.
**Recommendation:** Hold/comment, do not disqualify - genuinely strong clinical background with kids, but confirm her specific license type (LMHC/LCSW/LMFT vs. school-psychology credential) and Spanish fluency before deciding either way; I don't have enough to call this one confidently.

name: Mindy kissel
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong general full-cycle recruiting fundamentals; behavioral-health specificity is unclear.
**Strengths:** 5+ years full-cycle healthcare recruiting averaging 30 hires/month with a 1-2 week time-to-fill; HR coordination and compliance background; led a team of 30 at Kaiser Permanente.
**Gaps:** No Spanish; title is "Clinical Healthcare" recruiter broadly, not confirmed behavioral-health-specific; CA-based (FL residency is a preferred, not required, item).
**Recommendation:** Already past Applied stage - comment only. Solid recruiting operator; worth confirming behavioral-health-specific placement experience directly.

name: Chris Perry
review:
**Fit summary:** Not a fit for this role - a 30-year behavioral-health clinical/operations executive with zero recruiting experience anywhere in his history.
**Strengths:** Genuinely exceptional behavioral-health domain expertise (LPC, crisis systems, CARF accreditation, multi-site clinical operations) - just not for this function.
**Gaps:** No full-cycle recruiting, sourcing, ATS, or candidate-pipeline experience in any role listed; every position is clinical directorship, crisis-services executive leadership, or accreditation surveying.
**Recommendation:** Disqualify for this recruiter role - missing the core required qualification (2+ years of recruiting experience) entirely. Worth flagging separately to Devanne: his clinical-operations background is strong enough that it may be worth keeping on file for a completely different (clinical leadership) opening, not this one.

name: Marie Augustin
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong general full-cycle recruiter with FL residency; behavioral-health-specific recruiting experience is the one open gap.
**Strengths:** 10+ years full-cycle recruiting across staffing, hospitality, and mortgage; Florida-based; conversational Spanish; comp ask ($22/hr) in range; currently doing full-cycle recruiting work.
**Gaps:** No behavioral-health, mental-health, or substance-use recruiting named specifically in any role - her industries are staffing, hospitality, and mortgage.
**Consistency check:** None apparent.
**Tenure/timeline notes:** Two current-looking roles with overlapping end dates (Sept 2026) - "Talent Acquisition" and "HR Administrator/Hiring Manager" at different employers both ending now - worth a quick clarifying question on which is her actual current role.
**Recommendation:** Phone screen - real full-cycle recruiting strength and FL residency; the missing BH-specific experience is a fair question to explore rather than a disqualifier, since the core recruiting function is clearly there.

name: Chris Perry
review:
**Fit summary:** Duplicate application entry - same candidate and profile as above.
**Strengths:** See above.
**Gaps:** See above.
**Recommendation:** Disqualify (duplicate of candidate_id d585ebcdf302) - same reasoning: no recruiting experience against a role that requires it.

name: Jason Cantwell
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong high-volume recruiting track record, but entirely outside healthcare/behavioral health (DoD, IT, federal contracting).
**Strengths:** Senior Team Lead of Recruitment growing headcount from 350 to 450 contractors; consistent quota/above-quota performance across multiple recruiting agencies; comfortable with AI-assisted sourcing tools.
**Gaps:** No healthcare or behavioral-health recruiting anywhere in his history (DoD, IT, finance, manufacturing); basic Spanish only; 18-month contract ending is a clear, reasonable explanation for the job search.
**Recommendation:** Already past Applied stage - comment only. Excellent recruiting operator, but confirm directly whether he has any interest in or exposure to clinical/behavioral-health hiring before advancing, since it's a genuine gap.

name: Dina Hussein
review:
**Fit summary:** General healthcare-staffing recruiting background (nurses/caregivers); not confirmed behavioral-health-specific.
**Strengths:** Currently a Healthcare Recruiter at Maxim Healthcare Services running full-cycle recruiting for nurses and caregivers; familiar with multiple ATS platforms (RecruitCare, Bullhorn).
**Gaps:** Basic Spanish only; no behavioral-health-specific recruiting named; comp expectation listed as "0" which looks like a data-entry issue worth clarifying rather than an actual answer.
**Recommendation:** Already past Applied stage - comment only. Reasonable general healthcare-recruiting fit; clarify comp expectations and behavioral-health exposure directly.

name: Melissa M Cowman
review:
**Fit summary:** Notable early-career behavioral-health credentialing exposure alongside solid full-cycle agency and corporate recruiting experience.
**Strengths:** Associate degree in Chemical Dependency plus explicit "behavioral mental health credentialing (JCAHO)" experience early in her career; full-desk agency and corporate recruiting background; understands documentation/process requirements for credentialing health providers.
**Gaps:** No Spanish; her most recent 7+ year role (Talent Acquisition Specialist) doesn't appear to be behavioral-health-specific (industrial equipment company); reduction-in-force departure is a clear, non-concerning reason.
**Recommendation:** Already past Applied stage - comment only. The chemical-dependency/credentialing background is a genuine and somewhat unique plus worth exploring directly in her next conversation.

name: GARY WOODSON
review:
**Fit summary:** Cover letter describes directly relevant behavioral-health and child-psych recruiting background, but there's no structured work history to verify it against.
**Strengths:** Per his cover letter: 10+ years of healthcare recruiting including behavioral health, plus an unusual and relevant early career in Occupational Therapy and 2.5 years in child psych at Ohio State University Hospital.
**Gaps:** No Spanish; the structured work-history data is entirely empty - every claim here comes from the cover letter alone, with no employer/dates/title entries to cross-reference. [VERIFY] all of this against an actual resume before proceeding.
**Consistency check:** Can't run one - there's nothing structured to compare the cover-letter narrative against.
**Recommendation:** Disqualify for this batch is NOT appropriate given how relevant the narrative is if true - instead, request a complete resume/work history before screening further; the background described would be a strong fit if verified.

name: Jeffrey Gutierrez
review:
**Fit summary:** Solid general recruiting background in travel healthcare staffing; not behavioral-health-specific, and a chunk of his career is unrelated sales.
**Strengths:** Currently National Recruiter for travel healthcare therapy clinicians, growing placements to 45 within two years at 150% of target; fluent bilingual; comp ask ($25/hr) exactly matches the posted rate.
**Gaps:** Travel-therapy staffing isn't confirmed behavioral-health-specific; roughly half his work history (UCF Athletics, Miami Marlins) is ticket/premium-seating sales, unrelated to recruiting or healthcare.
**Consistency check:** A few "Title Unknown"/blank entries with overlapping dates (2018-2024 spans covering multiple roles) suggest some resume-parsing gaps rather than real overlaps - not a red flag on its own.
**Tenure/timeline notes:** Reasonable career progression; no concerning short-stay pattern.
**Recommendation:** Already past Applied stage - comment only. Bilingual and comp-aligned; his sales background could translate well to the relationship-building side of recruiting, worth exploring directly.
